newsitem.title: USA: India has no plan to ease capital controls further.
newsitem.headline: India has no plan to ease capital controls further.

text.p: India does not intend to further relax capital controls in the near future, Finance Minister Palaniappan Chidambaram said on Wednesday.
"We are not close at all because we don't feel the compulsion to do that," he told reporters during the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
"We have to wait for a suitable time when we have gained mastery over BOP (balance of payments) and our reserves have reached very comfortable levels," he said
"It is something we should introduce in stages. It is not something you should do overnight."

"Complete freedom with respect to capital transactions must be approached cautiously since many developing economies may have limited abilities to deal with volatility of capital flows, and capital flight may occur in crisis situations."

The government is trying encourage new foreign investment and strengthen its capital markets, he said. India has targetted $10 billion in direct foreign investment over the next four to five years, compared to to $2 billion last year.
It estimates it will need $150 billion in total to revamp its infrastructure, most of it coming from local sources.
Chidambaram reiterated that he wanted to bring the central government fiscal deficit, as a percentage of GDP, down to 4 percent from more than five percent at the moment.
Including state governments, the total deficit was nine percent, Chidambaram said, adding that it was up to the states to sort out their financial position.
He added that India had no plans to seek a medium programme from the IMF.
